paras: The threatened lynching of Joseph Warsaw took place in Warsaw, Illinois, in mid-March 1881, when citizens of the town threatened to lynch a man accused of assaulting a young woman. The authorities removed him to Carthage for safety, and no attack on him was reported. The episode is known from a single brief in the Cairo Bulletin, which did not state the man's race.

According to the Daily Cairo Bulletin of March 19, 1881, a man named Joseph Warsaw was accused of assaulting a young lady named Flachs in Warsaw, Illinois, "day before yesterday," or about March 17. The paper wrote that "the citizens of the place threatened to lynch him" but gave no number and did not describe a crowd gathering. The authorities then moved the accused to Carthage, the brief said, "for safety."
No report of a trial or any later proceedings against the accused appears in the coverage. The accused's name is printed as identical to the town's, which may reflect an error in the report.

The Cairo Bulletin ran the item as a single sentence among its local paragraphs, between a notice of plants for sale and a correction about a church lecture. It stated the assault as fact rather than as an accusation and called the accused "the brute," while reporting the threat of lynching without comment. The brief named no race for anyone involved, and no other white paper and no Black paper carried the story in the coverage found.
